newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos orders the arrest of Lawrence Wang, a suspected member of the Hong Kong 14-K Triad drug syndicate who was recently acquitted of charges of possession of drugs and unlicenced firearms. (MALAYA)
- The House committee on constitutional amendments files a resolution convening Congress into a constituent assembly that will discuss possible changes in the Constitution. (MANILA TIMES)
- The Commission on Elections reports a moderate turnout of new registrants for the local district elections to be held on May 12. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The presidential palace assures the public that there is no whitewash in the investigation of the land transaction between the Public Estate Authority and a private developer. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The Cabinet decides to include sugar in the Common Effective Preferential Tariff scheme, trade secretary Cesar Bautista says. (MANILA TIMES)
- The Makati Regional Trial Court lifts the garnishment order on banks involved in the Victorias Milling Co Inc debt problem. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Japanese trading giant Sumitomo Corp is planning to invest in carrageenan processing business in the southern Mindanao region, Sumitomo general manager Takeshi Seki says. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- Construction giant DM Consunji Inc and Itochu Corp of Japan have entered into a joint venture to develop a residential project in Cavite, just south of Manila. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
